title: Constructing a graduate employability knowledge graph with multi-source data fusion and graph neural network-based multi-task prediction
abstract: Addressing the limitations of existing employability prediction frameworks in cross-domain data integration and heterogeneous knowledge modelling, this study proposes a graduate employability knowledge graph construction framework grounded in multi-source heterogeneous data fusion and graph neural networks. A bidirectional confidence-scored alignment strategy is employed to integrate learning behaviour, market demand, and knowledge mastery data across three cross-domain sources, constructing a dynamic knowledge graph encompassing student, skill, and occupation entities across three hierarchical layers with seven semantically distinct relation types. An end-to-end multi-task prediction architecture incorporating basis decomposition parameter sharing and a dual-level attention mechanism is further developed upon this foundation. Experimental results validate the technical effectiveness of the proposed framework across skill mastery prediction, competency-level assessment, and job matching recommendation subtasks, as well as its representational stability under cross-dataset transfer conditions. The present study contributes a reproducible methodological framework for multi-source heterogeneous knowledge graph construction and graph-based multi-task prediction in educational contexts, with the findings offering a technical foundation for the design of intelligent career guidance systems and establishing a methodological basis for subsequent empirical investigations incorporating authentic graduate employment outcome data.

title: Sentiment analysis and satisfaction evaluation of ecotourism consumption under a multi-source deep learning framework
abstract: Ecotourism promotes sustainable development, but evaluating tourists’ experiences becomes difficult because of different multi-source feedback. Traditional methods using text or rating have been inaccurate. Research incorporates textual reviews and numerical ratings to enhance precision, depth and interpretability in ecotourism sentiments and satisfaction evaluation. The primary goal is to develop and validate an intelligent multi-source framework capable of robust sentiment classification and satisfaction prediction. To achieve this, this research proposes a Green Anaconda Optimized Long Short-Term Transformer Memory (GAO-LSTR) model that integrates the established LSTM–Transformer hybrid model with Green Anaconda Optimization (GAO) to improve parameter optimization, contextual feature learning, and multi-source sentiment classification performance. Multi-source data is gathered from ecotourism platforms, online review systems, and social media sources, including the Ecotourism Sentiment and Satisfaction Dataset. Text preprocessing includes tokenization and stop-word removal. TF-IDF is used for textual feature vectorization, while BERT is utilized to generate contextualized semantic embeddings from textual reviews, capturing deep linguistic and contextual relationships for improved feature representation. Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) layers capture sequential linguistic patterns, and Transformer components model long-range dependencies. The GAO is employed to optimize the hyperparameters of the LSTR, while network weights are learned through Adam-based backpropagation, thereby improving convergence stability, robustness, and predictive performance. The framework is implemented in Python using TensorFlow and PyTorch. On the benchmark Ecotourism Sentiment and Satisfaction Dataset containing structured sentiment annotations, the proposed GAO-LSTR model achieved an accuracy of 98.13% for sentiment classification and 79% for the satisfaction prediction task. The combined usage of textual and numerical characteristics guarantees high robustness, better interpretability, and consistently high prediction quality. The framework significantly enhances ecotourism sentiment and satisfaction evaluation by effectively integrating heterogeneous data modalities. The GAO-LSTR model provides a scalable and reliable solution for real-world ecotourism analytics, supporting improved decision-making and promoting sustainable tourism development.

title: TGSR: Text-Grounded Diffusion for Faithful Image Super-Resolution
abstract: Diffusion models have achieved remarkable success in image super-resolution (SR) by leveraging strong generative priors to enhance perceptual quality. However, for textual content, these priors often produce text hallucinations: non-existent or distorted text, which alter scene semantics and compromise model reliability. While recent methods focus on enhancing text generation, they do so indiscriminately, leaving hallucinations fundamentally unresolved. We argue the core problem is a lack of selective control. Therefore, we reformulate text SR as a selective generation problem: text is resolved only when reliable generation is expected, while other scene content is fully super-resolved. We introduce TGSR (Text-Grounded Super-Resolution), a test-time framework that progressively identifies and suppresses likely hallucinated text regions during generation. To enable this, we train dedicated detectors on a large-scale dataset curated from diverse diffusion-based SR outputs. TGSR consistently improves text fidelity across multiple backbones, increasing recognition precision by up to 17.68 points without degrading perceptual quality, underscoring the value of selective control in generative SR.

title: Personalization Without Stereotyping: Do Speech LLMs Know When to Turn a Deaf Ear?
abstract: Recent speech LLMs can leverage rich paralinguistic cues, enabling more complex and personalized interactions. However, little work investigates how this sensitivity can lead to stereotyping, and existing evaluations largely measure demographic disparities without distinguishing beneficial personalization from stereotypical behavior. We introduce BASIS-Bench, a benchmark designed to disentangle these two aspects through three axes: (1) demographic robustness, measuring disparities in content-based tasks across speakers and demographic classification capabilities; (2) stereotypical bias, measuring whether perceived demographic cues trigger unprompted stereotypical behavior; and (3) personalization, measuring whether models can tailor responses to demographic characteristics when explicitly requested. We evaluate eight recent speech LLMs and find that, despite often recognizing demographic cues, most fail to translate them into appropriate personalization. Explicit demographic labels improve personalization but also amplify stereotypical associations already present in the textual backbones. These findings highlight the need to train speech LLMs not only to perceive demographic cues, but to learn when they should shape their responses.

title: PRIME: Pre-Retrieval Index Modeling Enhancement for Structured Document Retrieval-Real
abstract: High-precision retrieval over external knowledge bases is essential for LLM agents to operate effectively. However, existing Information Retrieval (IR) research primarily optimizes query-side retrievers (e.g., ColBERT, BGE) and generators (e.g., Self-RAG, GraphRAG), while reducing corpus-side representation to chunking. This leaves index-side quality an underexplored lever. We propose Pre-Retrieval Index Modeling & Enhancement (PRIME), an index-side optimization framework built on two complementary tracks: an LLM-driven Semantic Restructuring (SR) track that transforms long documents into structured, information-dense sections, and a deterministic Metadata Synthesis (MS) and Hierarchical Retrieval (HR) track that extracts semantic anchors and heading structure for coarse-to-fine section retrieval. Our evaluations show that deterministic metadata matches structure-aware chunking's retrieval quality while cutting embedding computation by 45.8 $\times$ and index vector count by 22.4 $\times$. On top of these gains, Semantic Restructuring (SR) further improves Answer-F1 by 13.7% in full deployment, with characterized quality-fidelity-cost trade-offs. Across QASPER, BRIGHT, and NFCorpus, we further characterize three qualitative regimes that determine whether index-side optimization helps or degrades retrieval, while showing that these index-side effects are neutralized under a strong reranker.

title: Structure-Aware Matching for Robust UAV Thermal-to-Satellite Geo-Localization
abstract: UAV thermal-to-satellite geo-localization localizes UAVs by matching real-time thermal images against georeferenced satellite images, enabling autonomous navigation in GNSS-denied and low-visibility conditions. However, substantial cross-modal disparities in color, brightness and viewpoint hinder conventional appearance-based methods from establishing reliable correspondences. While existing approaches predominantly address global modality shifts, they overlook the invariant scene structures inherently shared between thermal and satellite views. To bridge this gap, we propose SAMF, a Structure-Aware Matching Framework that explicitly exploits stable cross-modal structural cues to improve UAV thermal geolocalization. Specifically, the Directional Structure Enhancement Module (DSEM) strengthens robust structural representations by capturing directional and low-frequency spatial patterns, and the Modality-Aware Affine Remapping Module (MARM) subsequently applies affine correction to these enhanced features, further promoting cross-modal alignment. Additionally, we introduce the Thermal-UAV-Paired benchmark derived from the Thermal-UAV dataset. Extensive experiments on both the Boson-nighttime and Thermal-UAV-Paired datasets show that SAMF achieves state-of-the-art performance. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness and synergistic complementarity of DSEM and MARM. The code and dataset are released at: https://github.com/YuxinWang879/SAMF.git.

title: Hybrid hypergraph networks for multimodal sequence data classification
abstract: Abstract Modeling temporal multimodal data requires both long-range temporal dependencies and cross-modal interactions to be represented. Existing approaches commonly model each modality separately and then apply shallow fusion, which can limit the representation of higher-order temporal structure. We propose a hybrid hypergraph network (HHN) that combines an established order-preserving alignment for candidate cross-modal links with an entropy-guided mechanism for constructing intra-modal hyperedges. Timestamped segments are represented as nodes; within each modality, an adaptive temporal window and a maximum-entropy-difference rule form higher-order hyperedges that are aggregated by hypergraph convolution. Across modalities, temporally weighted pairwise links and graph attention provide cross-modal fusion. Across four processed multimodal datasets, the reported mean average precision and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve were higher for HHN than for the evaluated baselines. Ablation results further indicate that both the hybrid graph modules and multimodal inputs contribute to classification performance.

title: 권기원_통합연구논문_2026-10-08
abstract: This conceptual and design-oriented study explores how artificial intelligence can support a context-sensitive understanding of human emotions, dispositions, intentions, circumstances, and processes of awareness. Drawing on personal reflection and AI system development, the author proposes a five-dimensional framework for human understanding and the concept of Jeoksim (適心), or context-sensitive selection of interpersonal attitudes. The study emphasizes evidence-based judgment, counterevidence, and iterative reassessment. It does not claim that AI possesses human-like feelings or consciousness. The proposed framework remains preliminary and requires future empirical validation.

title: ResNet-50-XGBoost Based Hybrid Model for Detection and Classification of Breast Cancer in Histopathology Imaging
abstract: Breast cancer continues to be the main cancer type which threatens women’s lives across all countries while creating a significant number of cancer deaths. The medical field requires immediate and accurate assessment of biopsy histopathological images which must be divided into benign and malignant categories to improve patient care through early medical intervention. The research introduces a novel system which uses deep learning techniques together with ensemble learning techniques to conduct breast cancer histopathological image classification for its binary classification task using BreakHis dataset. The proposed method establishes ResNet50 as an everlasting feature extractor which produces 2048dimensional deep feature vectors from microscopic tissue images through its Global Average Pooling (GAP) function after being pretrained on ImageNet.

title: CoMA: Condition-Modulated Context–Knowledge Attention for Empathetic Dialogue Generation
abstract: Empathetic response generation requires a model to balance emotional appropriateness with contextual grounding. However, the performance of emotion recognition remains relatively limited, which may lead to cascading errors in generating empathetic responses. To avoid error propagation from inaccurate emotion prediction and exploit emotion information more effectively, we propose CoMA (Condition-Modulated Context–Knowledge Attention), an empathetic response generation framework that uses condition from emotion and context representations as modulation signals during decoding. The condition representation is transformed into modulation weights to adjust attention logits, enabling the model to regulate the selectivity of the attention distributions over dialogue context and commonsense knowledge. In addition, CoMA employs a multi-decoder architecture with two separate branches for context and knowledge, whose representations are then fused to generate the final response. Experiments on the EmpatheticDialogues dataset show that CoMA achieves better performance than baseline models in both automatic and human evaluations. On EmpatheticDialogues, CoMA achieves a PPL of 20.47, BLEU of 2.72, Dist-1 of 0.86, and Dist-2 of 4.12. We further conduct an additional evaluation on the ESConv dataset, where CoMA obtains a PPL of 46.80, BLEU of 2.19, Dist-1 of 0.79, and Dist-2 of 3.13. These results indicate that using reliable emotional and contextual information to modulate attention, together with separate context–knowledge decoding, is effective for empathetic response generation across different conversational settings.

title: A multi-strategy fusion improved whale optimization algorithm for robot path planning
abstract: To address path planning for robots in grid environments, this study develops an improved whale optimization algorithm by integrating several complementary search strategies. The proposed method combines mixed initialization, a nonlinear convergence factor, adaptive inertia weight, Lévy-flight perturbation, and an A*-based local repair strategy to improve search ability and path feasibility. Tent chaotic mapping and an A*-based reference path are used to enhance population diversity and initialization quality, while the nonlinear and adaptive mechanisms balance exploration and exploitation. Experiments on 20×20 and 30×30 grid maps compare IWOA with representative metaheuristic algorithms, improved WOA variants, and classical planners. The results show that IWOA achieves competitive performance in path length, fitness value, collision avoidance, obstacle clearance, and convergence efficiency. The ablation results further demonstrate the effectiveness of the key components.

title: ELMA: Benchmarking Anaphoric Compositions for Long-Term Text-to-Motion Generation
abstract: Text-guided long-term human motion generation is essential for applications such as continuously operating digital avatars. Despite recent progress on short clips, existing models struggle with multi-segment instructions that involve anaphora, where constraints established in earlier segments must be preserved over time. In this paper, we introduce a novel task of long-term motion generation from such anaphoric compositions. To mitigate this, we present ELMA, an episodic long-term motion dataset with dense segment-level annotations that preserve cross-segment dependencies. Built via a fully automated collection and filtering pipeline, ELMA extracts high-quality, continuous 30-second clips from in-the-wild videos, capturing the episodic narratives necessary for long-range state modeling. Leveraging this dataset, we fine-tune state-of-the-art motion generation models to incorporate long-range context. Extensive experiments reveal fundamental shortcomings in current models when handling context-dependent instructions. We demonstrate that ELMA enables significant improvements in both global physical realism and semantic alignment, setting a robust new baseline for long-term motion synthesis.

title: Recovering Irreducible Three-Body Interactions with Lagrangian Neural Networks
abstract: Lagrangian Neural Networks (LNNs) learn mechanical systems from trajectory data by parameterizing a scalar Lagrangian and deriving the dynamics through the Euler-Lagrange equations, biasing the model toward motion that respects the variational structure of mechanics. The interactions studied so far have been pairwise-additive, leaving open whether LNNs can recover an irreducible many-body interaction from motion alone. We address this using the Axilrod-Teller triple-dipole interaction, the leading three-body dispersion term, whose dependence on the collective geometry of three particles cannot be represented by any sum of pairwise terms. We prescribe the kinetic energy exactly and learn only the potential, as a function of interparticle distances and angles. Combined with a signal-aware sampling strategy that concentrates training data where the three-body signal is strongest while preserving broad coverage of configuration space, this recovers the interaction from accelerations alone. The learned potential reproduces the radial scaling, angular dependence, and characteristic sign reversal of the Axilrod-Teller interaction, and generates stable trajectories. Embedding it within a pairwise Lennard-Jones potential lets us examine its observability: the three-body term is recovered once its dynamical signature exceeds the residual modeling error, which it does cleanly at amplified coupling but not at the coupling of a real noble gas, bracketing the transition between the two. Finally, symbolic regression on the trained potential, with no assumed functional form, returns the Axilrod-Teller expression with angular numerator, radial law, and coupling constant intact. An LNN with domain-specific structure can thus recover an irreducible three-body interaction from trajectories as a closed-form law, pointing toward learning interaction laws whose structure is not known a priori.

title: A4-MR: Abnormality-aware Anatomical Alignment for MR
abstract: Recent advances in large-scale foundation models have enabled strong generalization across a wide range of clinical and research tasks in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). However, existing vision-language MRI models remain limited in anatomy-specific localization and pathology-aware representation, particularly in real-world settings. We introduce A4-MR, a 3D vision-language foundation model trained on approximately 50,000 MRI studies comprising 491,000 series, roughly half of which are paired with radiology reports. A4-MR is designed to: (1) learn anatomy localization through large-scale pretraining with noisy labels; (2) align image and text representations at the anatomical level; and (3) learn distinct representations of healthy and abnormal anatomy. Across a diverse set of downstream tasks, A4-MR outperforms existing foundation models, including a +1.7 AUROC improvement over MedSigLIP for abnormality detection. Using a frozen encoder, A4-MR also surpasses an end-to-end task-specific MedNeXt model for knee segmentation by +1.4 Dice and performs comparably to the best task-specific model for abdominal organ segmentation on AMOS, within 0.4 Dice. Finally, without anatomical prompts, A4-MR localizes 3D anatomy comparably to MedSAM2 provided with ground-truth bounding boxes. Together, these results demonstrate that anatomy-level multimodal alignment and abnormality-aware representation learning can enable a single MRI foundation model to support localization, segmentation, and pathology-related tasks.

A4-MR is designed to: (1) learn anatomy localization through large-scale pretraining with noisy labels; (2) align image and text representations at the anatomical level; and (3) learn distinct representations of healthy and abnormal anatomy. Across a diverse set of downstream tasks, A4-MR outperforms existing foundation models, including a +1.7 AUROC improvement over MedSigLIP for abnormality detection. Using a frozen encoder, A4-MR also surpasses an end-to-end task-specific MedNeXt model for knee segmentation by +1.4 Dice and performs comparably to the best task-specific model for abdominal organ segmentation on AMOS, within 0.4 Dice. Finally, without anatomical prompts, A4-MR localizes 3D anatomy comparably to MedSAM2 provided with ground-truth bounding boxes. Together, these results demonstrate that anatomy-level multimodal alignment and abnormality-aware representation learning can enable a single MRI foundation model to support localization, segmentation, and pathology-related tasks.

title: Towards Robust Deep Reinforcement Learning against Environmental State Perturbation
abstract: Abstract Adversarial attacks and robustness in Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) have been widely studied in various threat models; however, few consider environmental state perturbations, which are natural in embodied scenarios. To improve the robustness of DRL agents, we formulate the problem of environmental state perturbation, introducing a preliminary non-targeted attack method as a calibration adversary, and then propose a defense framework, named Boosted Adversarial Training (BAT), which first tunes the agents via supervised learning to avoid catastrophic failure and subsequently adversarially trains the agent with reinforcement learning. Extensive experimental results substantiate the vulnerability of mainstream agents under environmental state perturbations and the effectiveness of our proposed attack. The defense results demonstrate that while existing robust reinforcement learning algorithms may not be suitable, our BAT framework can significantly enhance the robustness of agents against environmental state perturbations across various situations.

title: A Semantic Framework for the Assessment and Management of Historic Timber Structures: Linking CIDOC CRM-Based Ontological Modelling and HBIM
abstract: The conservation of historic timber structures requires the continuous collection and updating of heterogeneous information related to both historical development and structural safety. Data coming from repeated maintenance surveys and on-site assessments are often fragmented, difficult to compare, and poorly structured for long-term use. This study proposes a semantic framework for the assessment and management of historic timber structures, whose applicability is demonstrated through its application to the timber roof structure of the San Marco Museum in Florence. The methodology defines the knowledge domain specific to historic timber structure assessment and formalises it through an ontological model aligned with the CIDOC Conceptual Reference Model (CRM) and its extensions CRMba and CRMsci. The ontology is implemented in Web Ontology Language (OWL) using the Protégé editor, populated with individual instances, and queried through SPARQL, while an HBIM environment provides the spatial and operational context for data organisation and visualisation. The two systems are linked through a shared identifier system. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework enables the structured integration and querying of heterogeneous diagnostic data, supporting their long-term management while preserving provenance, temporal context, and methodological information.

title: Coordinate-Free Hidden-State Diagnostics Measure In-Context Meaning Override.
abstract: A language model must sometimes follow a local convention that conflicts with a familiar meaning. The same flexibility can let misleading examples re-anchor the meaning of an unchanged literal prompt: a driving assistant told “turn left” to avoid an obstacle may then read it as “turn right,” and no check of the text itself would catch the change. In arithmetic, after seeing “85 - 62 = 147,” should a model answer “44 - 42” as 2 or 86? We study when such contextual examples override a prior meaning and what hidden states reveal about that change. Controlled arithmetic, word, and command experiments in three open-weight models show substantial variation in resistance. In the open-ended arithmetic task, abandoning a prior interpretation need not mean adopting its replacement. We formulate hidden-state diagnostics using a covariance metric and a Fisher pullback, prove affine-invariance results, and derive an unbiased squared-distance estimator and an exact one-sided sign-flip test under stated assumptions. Experiments with the covariance metric reveal contextual effects that final answers alone can miss. Exploratory readout analyses and interventions, extended to two additional models, show reproducible readout alignment and model-dependent causal organization.

title: TALABALAR YOZMA ISHLARIDAGI GRAMMATIK XATOLARNI O'ZBEK TILIDA AVTOMATIK ANIQLASH VA TUZATISH TIZIMINING YETISHMASLIGI
abstract: Ushbu maqolada talabalarning o‘zbek tilidagi yozma ishlarida uchraydigan grammatik xatolarni avtomatik aniqlash va tuzatish muammosi ko‘rib chiqiladi. Hozirgi kunda ingliz va rus tillari uchun bunday tizimlar yetarlicha rivojlangan bo‘lsa-da, o‘zbek tili uchun bunday vosita amalda deyarli mavjud emas. Tadqiqotda mavjud xalqaro tajribalar tahlil qilinib, o‘zbek tilining morfologik xususiyatlari sababli yuzaga keladigan qiyinchiliklar aniqlandi. Natijada, qoidaga asoslangan va statistik usullarni birlashtirgan gibrid yondashuv taklif etildi. Ushbu yechim ta’lim muassasalarida amaliy jihatdan joriy etilishi mumkin. Xulosa qilib aytganda, milliy tilga moslashtirilgan grammatika tekshiruvchisi ta’lim sifatini oshirishda muhim vosita bo‘la oladi.

title: QSNA: Base-Conditioned Low-Rank Residual Refinement for Retention-Constrained Open-Vocabulary Detection on ROADWork
abstract: Adapting an open-vocabulary detector to work-zone imagery can improve target recognition but may reduce performance on source-domain and large-vocabulary benchmarks, represented here by COCO and LVIS. Replay and model merging can produce retention-aware checkpoints, but they do not by themselves provide a dedicated local refinement step after checkpoint selection. We propose Query Spectral-Null Adapter (QSNA), a complementary local update applied after checkpoint selection. QSNA freezes the selected checkpoint and learns an 8064-parameter low-rank residual at a single decoder FFN output projection, constrained by an estimated source-gradient complement. The residual can be rescaled after training and folded directly into the checkpoint. On the primary replay-derived checkpoint, QSNA raised ROADWork AP from 28.18 to 28.30, a +0.12 AP change, while COCO and LVIS AP decreased by 0.09 and 0.16 relative to the base. Across three fixed-base adapter seeds, the primary configuration produced similar descriptive ROADWork changes of about +0.13 AP and all three seeds remained above the adopted retention floors; this is replication evidence, not a significance test. Across nine base-specific fits, ROADWork AP repeatedly rose over a finite residual-scale range and then turned over, with the feasible range governed by the starting checkpoint. Canonical random, unconstrained, and projection-removed controls show that update orientation changes the acquisition–retention response, but they do not establish spectral projection as necessary or universally superior. Together, these results position QSNA as a base-conditioned, deployment-oriented local refinement stage after retention-aware checkpoint construction.

title: Echo: Error-Compensated 4-Bit Tensor-Parallel Communication for LLM Training and Inference
abstract: Tensor parallelism ends every layer with an all-reduce that sits between two dependent matrix multiplications, so its cost cannot be hidden and grows as compute outpaces interconnect bandwidth. Sending 4-bit instead of 16-bit values would cut this cost by nearly 4x, but the all-reduce must add the values it carries, and rounding the sum injects an error at every call. Model quality depends on how these errors accumulate over layers, yet existing methods treat each call on its own. We present Echo, a 4-bit all-reduce for training and inference that controls the accumulated error. Echo moves data in 4 bits and sums in high precision, so each value is quantized at most twice per call for any number of GPUs. The summation reveals each injected error, and Echo feeds it back into later calls, so old errors cancel instead of accumulating. We prove that the accumulated error stays bounded independently of depth. On A100 GPUs, Echo is 2.09x faster than the 16-bit NCCL all-reduce on 1 GB messages. It speeds up the time to first token by up to 1.16x and the training step by up to 1.09x on an idle interconnect, and by up to 1.44x and 1.38x as background traffic grows. It keeps the average accuracy over seven benchmarks within 0.4 points of 16-bit inference on Qwen3-8B. In 10B-token pretraining, its final loss is less than 0.9% above that of 16-bit training. Echo needs no FP8 or FP4 hardware.

title: Auditing VLM Benchmarks from Existing Evaluation Runs
abstract: Every evaluation run of a vision-language model (VLM) already produces per-question artifacts (predictions, judged correctness, metadata) that leaderboards reduce to a single score and then discard. We reuse those artifacts to audit the benchmark itself, and add an audit layer to VLMEvalKit: six detectors that run as post-processing over saved outputs, plus one additional text-only rerun with visual inputs removed, emitting a per-question report. The layer reports per-question findings together with aggregate audit statistics; for the headline quantities, it attaches permutation-null excess where applicable, interval estimates for proportions, and sensitivity to the model pool. Auditing MMStar, a benchmark curated specifically so that the image is indispensable, with three models, we find zero aggregate accuracy gain from the image on 20.2% of its questions. An item-matched permutation null accounts for 17.0%, leaving a +3.2 pp excess (corrected permutation p = 0.001). This excess is concentrated in the mathematics and science categories and is absent from coarse perception, a localization consistent with knowledge substituting for visual evidence; confirming that mechanism would require item-level review. A second detector flags 134 questions on which every model that answered in parseable form picked the same non-gold option, and these candidates peak in the perception categories, whereas the zero-gain excess is largest in mathematics and science & technology. Replacing the LLM judge with exact string matching changes no conclusion, and every scoring discrepancy between the two traces to one model whose free-form answers a parser cannot read. On a binary yes/no benchmark the detectors measurably fall out of calibration, a scope boundary that we measure and report. The audit layer, the prediction artifacts and the generated reports accompany this submission.

title: UniMergeTrack: Hierarchical Model Merging for General RGB-X Visual Object Tracking
abstract: RGB-X tracking leverages complementary modalities, such as thermal infrared, event, or depth, to improve robustness under challenging conditions. Existing general-purpose RGB-X trackers typically follow two paradigms: independent task-specific training and joint training across modality combinations. However, the former suffers from knowledge isolation and model redundancy, while the latter introduces optimization interference across heterogeneous tasks. In this work, we present UniMergeTrack, a new model merging paradigm that preserves task-specific optimization while enabling effective cross-task knowledge integration. UniMergeTrack first trains modality-specific trackers independently and then performs hierarchical model merging. Specifically, transferable backbones are merged across RGB-X tasks via high-pass-filtered merging, and complemented by lightweight task-specific experts that preserve modality-specific cues. Tracking heads are merged within each task using optimal transport-guided channel alignment to mitigate hidden channel mismatch. A subsequent distribution alignment fine-tuning stage further improves compatibility between the unified backbone and task-specific heads. Extensive experiments on the LasHeR, RGBT234, VisEvent, VOT-RGBD22, COESOT, and CDTB benchmarks demonstrate that UniMergeTrack achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance across RGB-Thermal, RGB-Event, and RGB-Depth tracking tasks, while exhibiting strong generalization to unseen datasets. The source code will be released upon acceptance. The source code of this paper will be released on https://github.com/Event-AHU/OpenEvTracking.

title: Reinforcement learning for adaptive composition of quantum circuit optimisation passes
abstract: Abstract Many quantum software development kits provide a suite of circuit optimisation passes. These passes have been highly optimised and tested in isolation. However, the order in which they are applied is left to the user, or else defined in general-purpose default pass sequences. While general-purpose sequences miss opportunities for optimisation which are particular to individual circuits, designing pass sequences bespoke to particular circuits requires exceptional knowledge about quantum circuit design and optimisation. Here we propose and demonstrate training a reinforcement learning agent to compose optimisation-pass sequences. In particular the agent's action space consists of passes for two-qubit gate count reduction used in default PyTKET pass sequences. For the circuits in our diverse test set, the (mean, median) fraction of two-qubit gates removed by the agent is (57.7%, 56.7%), compared to (41.8%, 50.0%) for the next best default pass sequence. In doing so our model demonstrates the ability to forgo reward to improve the final two-qubit gate count. Our approach clearly separates the problem of designing circuit optimisation passes from the problem of using them optimally in practice. We expect this separation of concerns to facilitate innovations in both areas.

title: Sentiment Analysis of Social Media Posts using FastText Embedding and a Hybrid BiLSTM-Attention-CNN Deep Learning Architecture
abstract: Looking into how people feel about things online now matters a lot when tracking what crowds think, how brands are seen, or spotting shifts in user actions across large groups. Most current methods lean heavily on models like BERT which are powerful at sorting sentiments yet slow to train and hungry for computing power. Instead of following that path, this study presents a simpler mix; it combines FastText with a BiLSTM layer that sees context both ways, adds a slim attention component that highlights key words, then feeds results into a CNN for final output. It grabs small word fragments with the help of FastText, tracks order in sequences using BiLSTM, uses attention to weigh meaningful parts more, while the CNN pinpoints sharp, useful patterns which others might overlook. Testing took place on two open Twitter sentiment datasets. One holds 74,682 labeled entries split into four categories: Positive, Negative, Neutral, Irrelevant. The other includes around 162,000 instances grouped under three labels: Positive, Negative, Neutral. Instead of relying on heavy transformer designs, the approach here keeps computation leaner but still matches standard accuracy levels. Performance stayed strong using a mix of BiLSTM-Attention for features and CNN for final predictions. Metrics like precision, recall, F1, accuracy, along with confusion matrices, confirmed consistency across tests. Both TensorFlowand PyTorch were used to build the system, allowing insights into differences between coding environments. Results point toward a balanced option that works well without demanding excessive resources for analyzing emotions in vast streams of social network posts.

title: Consumer Complaint Mining Through Topic Modeling and Sentiment Analysis: A Proof-of-Concept Analytical Framework for Decision Support
abstract: Consumer complaint narratives are an underused source of business and regulatory evidence. This study presents a proof-of-concept analytical framework for multi-dimensional complaint analysis and uncertainty-aware evidence synthesis, with potential use in human-in-the-loop decision support, and applies it to 99,434 Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) complaint records spanning from March 2015 to March 2026. The empirical workflow integrates BERTopic topic discovery, two pretrained sentiment checkpoints (ProsusAI/finbert and cardiffnlp/twitter-roberta-base-sentiment-latest), exploratory clustering of complaint records, and descriptive temporal summaries. A conceptual stock–flow and feedback representation links observed complaints, analytical alerts, response capacity, and unresolved issues; these relations are not causally estimated or simulated. BERTopic produced 89 non-outlier topics. A probability-based outlier-reassignment stage assigned 80.46% of records to these topics, while 19.54% remained unassigned and were retained as an uncertainty queue. A FinBERT-prediction-stratified benchmark of 600 complaint records was independently coded by two annotators (raw agreement = 87.5%; Cohen’s κ = 0.758). Against Annotator 1 as the prespecified reference, Cardiff RoBERTa aligned better with the labels on the prediction-stratified benchmark (κ = 0.395; sample accuracy = 67.3%) than FinBERT (κ = 0.195; sample accuracy = 46.3%), although neither model supports autonomous use. The four-group K-means solution is reported as exploratory because the highest observed Silhouette coefficient was only 0.106 and favored K = 2. Temporal patterns coincided with selected external events, but no causal effect is claimed. The contribution is therefore a transparent, uncertainty-aware analytical architecture whose potential organizational uses require human review and operational validation.

title: Analysis of Clustering Algorithms Using Minimum Spanning Tree with Different Threshold Values
abstract: Clustering analysis is a key research area in data mining because of its many uses. Although numerous clustering algorithms have been developed, each algorithm possesses its own strengths and limitations, and no signal algorithms perform well in real world scenarios. Among these approaches, the Minimum Spanning Tree (MST)- based clustering algorithms are widely used because of their capability to detect cluster with irregular shapes and boundaries. In this study, the MST based clustering algorithm is analyzed using different threshold values and its performance is measured using a validity index. Thresholds are determined using Mean, Standard Deviation (SD) and Mean + Standard Deviation (SD) of MST edge weights. Clusters are formed by selecting or removing edges from the MST based on these thresholds. The clustering performance is evaluated using a validity index (VI), defined as the ratio of intra-cluster distance and inter-cluster distance, where optimal threshold is identified by the minimum validity index. The proposed technique is implemented on both randomly generated datasets and as well as real-world datasets using python programming language. Experimental results demonstrate that the Mean + Standard Deviation (SD) threshold continuously on every dataset produces optimal clustering results with minimum validity index.

title: Development of an Expert System for Diagnosing Toddler Nutritional Status Using a Participatory Design Approach
abstract: Assessing the nutritional status of a toddler remains an essential challenge for child health, since the process often requires professional expertise and may not always be readily available to the community. This work presents a web-based expert system to assist in assessing toddler nutritional status by combining the Certainty Factor method with the Participatory Design methodology. Nutritionists, Posyandu (Integrated Health Post) cadres, and parents of toddlers were actively involved in the development process, from identifying user requirements to designing the system to evaluating its functionality. The knowledge base consisted of 24 symptoms and six categories of nutritional status, representing expert knowledge, and the Certainty Factor approach was used to address the uncertainty in the diagnostic procedure. The resulting system offers integrated capabilities for Z-Score calculation, symptom-based consultation, nutritional status diagnosis, and follow-up suggestions. The diagnostic validation was performed on 30 selected toddler records and showed promising performance with 88.30% accuracy, 89.98% precision, 88.30% recall, and 87.08% F1-score. Moreover, the usability test conducted with 50 respondents yielded an average System Usability Scale (SUS) score of 79.15, which falls within the Acceptable category, namely Grade B or Good adjective rating. The results of this study show that the proposed system can efficiently enable early diagnosis of children's nutritional status while offering a user-friendly experience and high user approval.

title: UkrMeme: Multimodal Explainable Persuasion Detection in Ukrainian Memes
abstract: Memes play a central role in modern online communication, especially in contexts of political conflict where visual and textual cues combine to convey persuasive messages. We study persuasive technique detection in Ukrainian memes using vision-language models (VLMs). We introduce UkrMeme, a dataset of 200 organically produced Ukrainian wartime memes annotated for persuasion techniques, and PTM-UA, a Ukrainian translation of a subset of the Propaganda 950 benchmark that preserves original visual content while translating meme text. We evaluate VLMs in a zero-shot prompting setup across image, text, and multimodal inputs using hierarchical F1 metrics. Finally, we compare Layer-wise Relevance Propagation (LRP) and model-generated token attributions and analyze the semantic categories of evidence emphasized by each explanation method.

title: MOSAIC: Multi-Scale Object-Centric Slot Adaptation with Image-Guided Prototype Conditioning for Remote Sensing Image Super-Resolution
abstract: Pretrained diffusion Transformers provide powerful generative priors for image restoration, yet adapting them to structure-sensitive tasks remains challenging. Existing methods mainly rely on dense low-resolution features as conditions, which often entangle salient objects with dominant backgrounds and provide limited abstraction for recurring structures across scales and samples. We propose MOSAIC, an object-centric representation learning framework that learns compact structural conditions for generative model adaptation. MOSAIC organizes degraded observations into structural slots that capture complementary object-level and layout-level evidence, integrates them across resolutions, and retrieves recurring priors from a shared prototype memory to complement incomplete image-specific information. The resulting representations are injected into selected layers of a frozen diffusion Transformer through lightweight residual modulation, preserving its pretrained generative prior. We instantiate MOSAIC for remote sensing image super-resolution, where small objects, repetitive structures, and large-scale variation provide a challenging testbed. Experiments on UCMerced, AID, and RSSCN7 show consistent PSNR improvements across $\times 2$ and $\times 4$ settings and favorable LPIPS results at $\times 4$. Qualitative results further demonstrate improved preservation of small objects, structural boundaries, and repetitive spatial patterns.

title: A Bayesian prevalence incidence cure model for estimating survival using electronic health records with incomplete baseline diagnoses
abstract: Retrospective cohorts can be extracted from electronic health records (EHRs) to study prevalence, time until disease or event occurrence, and cure proportion in real-world scenarios. However, EHRs are collected for patient care rather than research, and thus typically have complexities, such as patients with missing baseline disease status. Prevalence incidence (PI) models, which use a two-component mixture model to account for this missing data, have been proposed. However, PI models are biased in settings in which some individuals will never experience the endpoint (they are 'cured'). To address this, we propose a prevalence-incidence-cure (PIC) model, a three-component mixture model that combines the PI model framework with a cure model. Our PIC model enables estimation of the prevalence rate, time-to-incidence, and the cure proportion, and allows for covariate effects on each component. We adopt a Bayesian inference approach, and focus on the interpretability of the prior. We show in a simulation study that the PIC model has smaller bias than PI and cure models for the survival probability; and we compare inference under vague, informative and misspecified priors. We illustrate our PIC model using a dataset of 1964 patients who underwent treatment for diabetic macular oedema, and demonstrate improved fit under our model.

title: Karakterisasi Profil Endapan Nikel Laterit pada Bukit X dan Bukit Y PT Vale Indonesia Tbk
abstract: PT Vale Indonesia Tbk adalah sebuah perusahaan pertambangan nikel yang beroperasi di Sorowako, Kabupaten Luwu Timur, Provinsi Sulawesi Selatan. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengidentifikasi jenis mineral yang ada di setiap lapisan endapan nikel laterit, mengetahui komposisi mineral dalam batuan dasar, serta mengidentifikasi karakteristik kimia endapan nikel laterit pada Bukit X dan Bukit Y yang merupakan bagian dari PT Vale Indonesia Tbk. Data yang digunakan dalam penelitian berupa endapan nikel laterit yang terdiri dari lapisan limonit, saprolit, dan batuan dasar. Untuk menganalisisnya, digunakan metode X-Ray Diffraction (XRD), analisis petrografi, dan analisis X-Ray Flourescence (XRF). Hasil analisis XRD menunjukkan himpunan mineral pada lapisan limonit Bukit X terdapat mineral enstatite, hematite, dan ilmenite. Di lapisan saprolit Bukit X ditemukan mineral kuarsa, forsterite, dan hematite. Sementara itu, pada lapisan batuan dasar Bukit X ditemukan mineral antigorite, forsterite, enstatite, dan lizardite. Hasil analisis XRD menunjukkan himpunan mineral di Bukit Y, pada lapisan limonit ditemukan hematite-proto serta goethite. Di lapisan saprolit ditemukan forsterite dan enstatite. Lapisan batuan dasar Bukit Y mengandung forsterite, enstatite, antigorite, dan diopside. Hasil analisis petrografi yang dilakukan pada sampel lapisan batuan dasar Bukit X ditemukan mineral olivine terserpentinisasi, orthopyroxene, opaque, serta clinopyroxene dengan jenis batuan serpentinized lherzolite. Sementara itu, untuk hasil analisis petrografi pada sampel lapisan batuan dasar Bukit Y mengandung mineral olivine terserpentinisasi, orthopyroxene, serta clinopyroxene dengan jenis batuan serpentinized lherzolite. Hasil analisis X-Ray Flourescence (XRF) pada kedua bukit tersebut menunjukkan bahwa kadar MgO dan SiO2 meningkat dari lapisan limonit ke lapisan batuan dasar karena unsur Mg dan Si mudah tererosi akibat proses pelapukan. Sementara itu, kadar Fe, Co, Mn, Cr, dan Al2O3 menurun dari lapisan limonit ke lapisan batuan dasar karena unsur tersebut memiliki mobilitas yang rendah. Kandungan Ni mengalami penurunan secara bertahap dari lapisan limonit ke lapisan batuan dasar, tetapi meningkat di lapisan saprolit. Hal ini disebabkan oleh mobilitas Ni yang terbatas

title: A spatial AI-based biomarker with independent prognostic value in early low- and intermediate- risk breast cancer
abstract: Abstract Background Patients with ER-positive/HER2-negative early breast cancer of low or intermediate grade are generally considered to have a favourable prognosis, yet a number will recur. This risk is poorly captured by standard clinicopathological factors. AI-based medical devices for whole slide image (WSI) analyses used for risk-stratification often predict on slide-level thereby overlooking spatial localisation of the biomarkers. We hypothesise that the spatial distribution of a previously reported AI-based marker provides independent prognostic value beyond its global score. Patients and Methods This Swedish multicentre cohort study includes 6106 patients with primary invasive breast cancer: 3078 from the Stockholm region (training) and 3028 from Skåne (independent test). Tile-level high-grade morphology scores were generated with ViT_DG, a vision-transformer adaptation of DeepGrade, and the presence of clusters of high-risk tiles localised at the invasive tumour front was defined as a binary biomarker. Primary analyses were pre-specified in the ER-positive/HER2-negative/lymph-node-negative and Grade 1-2 subgroup. Association with breast-cancer recurrence-free interval (BCRFI) and distant metastasis were assessed using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models (HR). Results In the primary subgroup (n=1536 training; n=1403 test), tumour front clusters were present in 37% and 39% of patients. Cluster-positive status was associated with a 2.30-fold increased risk in the external test. Cluster-negative patients achieved a 10-year BCRFI of 95.3%, equivalent to Grade 1 patients and better than Grade 2 (92.4%), whereas cluster-positive patients (90.2%) did worse than the Grade 3 reference. The association was retained in patients classified as low-risk by ViT_DG (test set multivariable HR 2.86), identifying high-risk patients not captured by the global score. Conclusions The absence of high-risk morphology clusters at the tumour front is an independent prognostic indicator, identifying a low-risk group independently of the global AI biomarker classification. More broadly, preserving the spatial distribution of AI-derived predictions enables prognostic stratification beyond slide-level aggregation. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT02306096

title: WP-560 — Breaking Through: Advancements in Cryptography and Geometric Factor Authentication
abstract: Recent advancements in cryptography, particularly in quantum techniques and geometric factor authentication, raise significant questions concerning the viability of traditional cryptographic methods. This white paper explores the limitations of current cryptographic systems, the implications of vulnerabilities in cryptocurrencies, and our ability to leverage geometric factor authentication methodologies. It argues for the necessity of innovative technologies that can address these vulnerabilities and protect digital assets effectively.

title: Tutorial: Extracting Unstructured Text Using Large Language Models
abstract: This tutorial shows how to build a two-stage pipeline in which a multimodal large language model reads each page as an image and a second model turns the extracted text into structured JSON. We cover the choices that make such pipelines reliable and affordable, including structured outputs, parameter control, task decomposition, cost-effective model selection, and validation against a human-verified ground truth.

title: QLFL: quantum-enabled lightweight federated learning-empowered threat detection model for Internet of Medical Things based healthcare
abstract: The integration of Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) has significantly reshaped the landscape of modern healthcare, facilitating seamless communication between connected IoMT devices. Despite these advancements, the growing adoption of healthcare technologies has raised critical cybersecurity and data privacy concerns. Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered solutions have gained traction as an effective means to strengthen Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) against emerging cyber threats. Nevertheless, deploying AI-based IDS in healthcare environments presents obstacles, such as excessive computational overhead and the need for secure data handling. To address the above mentioned challenges, this article proposes Quantum Lightweight Federated Learning (QLFL), an innovative framework combining Quantum Computing (QC) and Federated Learning (FL) to deliver a high-performance, scalable, and privacy-centric intrusion detection system for IoMT networks. The proposed methodology adopts knowledge distillation techniques within FL to create an optimized detection model suitable for low-power devices. Moreover, Additive Homomorphic Encryption is implemented to safeguard model parameters during federated training, maintaining data confidentiality without compromising processing speed. Experimental evaluations highlight the system reliability, with accuracy rates of 98.90% on the IoT Healthcare Security dataset, demonstrating stable performance under varying network conditions. These findings suggest that QLFL could play a pivotal role in enhancing the cybersecurity framework for next-generation healthcare applications.

title: RoboFake: Are Deepfake Detectors Ready for Humanoid Face Robots?
abstract: Humanoid face robots can now move their lips in sync with speech and show detailed facial expressions. Give such a robot the face of a real person and drive it with generated speech, and you get a face forgery that happens in front of the camera: the camera records a real object, and no pixel is edited. We call this a RoboFake. In this paper we ask what current deepfake detectors do when they see a robot face. We test six public detectors trained on FaceForensics++ on video of a physical lip-syncing face robot, on a synthesized video of the same robot, and on rendered robot faces. All thresholds are fixed on FaceForensics++, and every result is compared with real human faces that went through the same processing as the robot videos. Our results suggest that current detectors flag today's robots because their faces do not look human, not because they recognize a forgery. We release our evaluation protocol and code, and state three testable hypotheses about realistic, interactive RoboFakes.

title: Efficient Confidence-Aware Densification for 3DGS
abstract: 3DGS-MCMC has replaced the gradient-driven density control of 3D Gaussian Splatting with opacity-based sampling and relocation, and is now the de facto standard for prior-free densification under a fixed primitive budget. Because opacity stays high where the scene is already well reconstructed, this sampling sends most new primitives to the foreground and leaves the background under-reconstructed. At low budgets, prior-based methods such as ConeGS and EDGS outperform it, at the cost of a pre-trained radiance field or dense image matches and a separate initialization stage. We argue for a comeback of error-driven densification within the fixed-budget MCMC framework. Our confidence-aware densification keeps the fixed budget and gradual growth of 3DGS-MCMC, but places primitives by the image error instead of the opacity. New primitives are drawn mostly where screen-space gradients are large. We favor primitives with a low learned confidence, which marks regions the reconstruction still explains poorly, and relocate the primitives that contribute least to the rendered images to these places. Averaged over 24 scenes, our method outperforms 3DGS-MCMC in PSNR, SSIM and LPIPS at every budget from 100k to 2M primitives. At 100k, without a prior or an initialization stage, it recovers 0.84dB of the 1.05dB PSNR by which ConeGS leads 3DGS-MCMC, and from 500k on, it has the highest PSNR and SSIM of all fixed-budget methods we compare with, including ConeGS and EDGS. While inherently prior-free, our densification can also exploit priors: from the ConeGS or EDGS initialization, it matches ConeGS in PSNR and SSIM at 100k and is best in all three metrics at 500k.

title: NOFACE3D: NOise-scheduled Focused Anchoring and Controlled Enhancement for 3D Generation
abstract: Recent image-to-3D models generate complete, high-quality assets from a single image, with global shape and appearance that are already convincing; what remains is the fine scale, where small, thin, elongated, or detail-rich regions are reconstructed softly and under-resolved. This gap can arise in generators with fixed-resolution spatial grids: the same spatial sampling density is used for a large, smooth, low-curvature surface and for a thin, high-curvature structure that carries most of the perceived detail. To this end, we introduce NOFACE3D, a training-free framework that refines these detail-critical regions while preserving the rest of the asset. Given a generated mesh, its input image, and a refinement box, NOFACE3D extracts the selected submesh, scales it up to fill the generator's input volume, and re-encodes it into the full-resolution latent grid. Conditioned on the image crop, it refines the region through flow-based sampling with a spatially varying noise schedule that anchors boundary latents. The refined region is then integrated back into the original asset, preserving the surrounding geometry and appearance. We implement NOFACE3D on TRELLIS.2 and its sparse voxel representation; all of it operates purely at inference time on the frozen pretrained generator. We evaluate NOFACE3D on PAniC-3D, TexVerse and BigDetail, a new benchmark of 339 assets with annotated detail-critical regions. On all three, it generates sharper geometry and finer texture detail than the baselines. Project page: https://idkcouscous.github.io/NoFACE3D/

title: When Charts Deceive Web Agents: A Paired Benchmark for Misleading Visualization-Grounded Tasks
abstract: Web agents increasingly browse, interpret, and act on web content on behalf of users. In many realistic workflows, however, the visual evidence they consume is not neutral: charts and dashboards can be misleading, shaping judgments without issuing any explicit malicious instruction. Unlike chart question answering, Web Agents treat charts as intermediate evidence whose misinterpretation can propagate into concrete downstream actions --- a reliability risk that remains underexplored. We introduce MisVisAgentBench, the first paired executable benchmark for evaluating how misleading visualizations affect Web Agent execution. It comprises 280 task instances in matched clean--misleading pairs that differ only in chart evidence. We further provide a diagnostic framework that isolates misleading-induced failures from baseline task difficulty (Zhu et al., 2025) and captures execution-level effects such as extra browsing steps and decision hesitation. Across thirteen vision-language Web Agents, replacing clean charts with misleading counterparts reduces the average task success rate by more than 34 percentage points. Moreover, these failures predominantly follow the targeted misleading action branch, suggesting that deceptive charts systematically redirect rather than randomly disrupt agent decisions. These results reveal that visualization robustness is a critical yet understudied dimension of Web Agent safety and reliability.

title: Fault-tolerant execution of error-corrected quantum algorithms
abstract: Scaling up quantum algorithms to tackle high-impact problems in science and industry requires quantum error correction and fault tolerance. While progress has been made in experimentally realizing error-corrected primitives, the end-to-end execution of logical quantum algorithms using only fault-tolerant (FT) components has remained out of reach. We demonstrate the FT and error-corrected execution of two quantum algorithms, the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) and the Harrow-Hassidim-Lloyd (HHL) algorithm applied to the Poisson equation, on Quantinuum H2 and Helios trapped-ion quantum processors using the $[[7,1,3]]$ Steane code. For QAOA circuits on 5 and 6 logical qubits, we show performance improvements from increasing the number of QAOA layers and the number of $T$ gates used to approximate logical rotations, despite increased physical circuit complexity. We further show that QAOA circuits with up to 8 logical qubits and 9 logical $T$ gates perform similarly to unencoded circuits. For the largest QAOA circuits we run, with 12 logical (97 physical) qubits and 2132 physical two-qubit gates, we still observe better-than-random performance. Finally, we show that adding active QEC cycles and increasing the repeat-until-success limit of state preparation subroutines can improve the performance of a quantum algorithm, thereby demonstrating critical capabilities of scalable FT quantum computation. Our results are enabled by an FT logical $T$ gate implementation with an infidelity of $\sim 2.6(4)\times10^{-3}$ and dynamic circuits with measurement-dependent feedback. Our work demonstrates near-break-even performance of complex, error-corrected algorithmic quantum circuits using only FT components.

title: AI-Powered Personalised Mobile Learning Using Large Language Models: Design, Implementation, and a Simulation-Based Feasibility Evaluation
abstract: The significance of mobile learning (m-learning) has been greatly highlighted by the advent of technology due to its flexibility, accessibility and capability of being used to learn at any time and place. The development of Large Language Models (LLMs) offers great potential for creating adaptive, conversational and content-aware learning experiences via mobile apps. Most existing mobile-learning systems, however, still provide largely static content and shallow personalisation, which limits sustained learner engagement and adaptive support. This paper presents the design and implementation of an Android-based, LLM-powered personalised m-learning platform that integrates four components: a conversational tutoring agent, an Item-Response-Theory (IRT)-based adaptive quiz engine, a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) content-recommendation module, and an analytics-driven feedback loop. We describe the system architecture, the prompt-orchestration and knowledge-tracing pipelines, and a rigorous quasi-experimental evaluation protocol (pre-/post-test, System Usability Scale (SUS), and engagement analytics) designed for a controlled classroom deployment. To validate the core algorithmic contributions prior to human-subject trials, we conduct two simulation-based feasibility studies: (i) a synthetic-learner simulation comparing the adaptive difficulty engine against a static item sequence and (ii) a retrieval-precision benchmark comparing RAG-based content recommendation against keyword-matching on a synthetic tagged corpus. The adaptive engine delivered quiz items within the optimal challenge zone (0.4 < P(correct) < 0.8) for 77.8% of interactions, compared with 40.8% for the static baseline, while the RAG recommender achieved substantially higher retrieval precision at every cut-off (P@10 = 0.845 versus 0.483 for keyword matching). These results provide algorithmic evidence that the proposed adaptive and retrieval components behave as intended and motivate the full-scale classroom evaluation described in the protocol. The paper concludes with a discussion of design implications, limitations, and a concrete plan for the human-subject study and future extensions of the platform.

title: Responsible AI- Enabled Innovation: A Conversation Starter for Victoria’s Innovation Ecosystem
abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly becoming a general-purpose capability for innovation. Victoria should ensure that founders and innovators across all sectors, not only AI-native startups, can use it to discover opportunities, develop and test ventures, improve productivity, and grow responsibly. This conversation starter proposes a practical agenda for inquiry and action. It invites innovators, investors, researchers, industry partners, universities, accelerators and government to work together to identify valuable applications, capability gaps, appropriate safeguards and effective support mechanisms for responsible AI-enabled innovation. AI can lower the time, cost and expertise required to research opportunities, generate concepts, develop prototypes and operate new ventures. However, faster experimentation does not necessarily produce stronger innovation. The opportunity is therefore not simply to increase AI adoption but to help innovators combine AI’s speed and reach with human judgement, domain expertise, engagement with users and affected communities, proportionate safeguards and clear accountability. AI use is expanding across Australian businesses and is particularly associated with innovation-active firms. At the same time, access to expertise, secure infrastructure, legal and intellectual-property advice, validation opportunities, mentors and investment networks remains uneven. Without coordinated action, well-resourced ventures may be better positioned to capture AI’s benefits, while smaller and under-supported innovators face greater risks of superficial adoption and preventable mistakes. Victoria already has significant research, sector, startup, commercialisation and investment capabilities. The immediate opportunity is to connect these existing strengths and build a responsible AI-enabled innovation layer across the ecosystem, not to create another standalone organisation or duplicate established programs. The immediate request is to convene interested partners to refine the agenda, identify priority sectors and use cases, determine suitable pilot opportunities, and agree on roles, resources and measures of success. The intended outcome is a practical foundation for helping Victorian innovators use AI to develop ventures that are differentiated, evidence-based, commercially credible, socially valuable and worthy of trust.

title: Spec2VEC : Interpretable Spectral Representations of Planetary Signals in Vector Spaces
abstract: Summary The application of machine learning to planetary geophysics is frequently bottlenecked by a scarcity of labeled data and the complexity of non-stationary seismo-acoustic signals. While deep learning offers powerful feature extraction, it requires massive datasets that are rarely available for phenomena like Martian quakes or deep-ocean volcanism. Consequently, researchers often rely on unsupervised machine learning or hand-engineered features that are typically impoverished or hard to interpret. To resolve this, we introduce Spec2VEC, a framework that transforms parameter-dependent TFRs into a robust, interpretable, and high-dimensional vector space. Spec2VEC treats spectrograms not merely as energy distributions but as structured, textured images, and extracts physics-informed, dataset-agnostic features without requiring massive training loops. The framework systematically extracts a feature vector using two novel pathways: (1) a Textural path that utilizes Hilbert space-filling curves to map 2D spectral patterns into 1D sequences for advanced information-theoretic analysis (e.g., permutation entropy, fractal dimension); and (2) a Spatial path driven by PDFSI (Probabilistic Distribution Fitting for Signal Identification), a novel probabilistic pre-conditioning engine that quantifies spatial connectivity by dynamically separating coherent signal modes from stochastic noise. We validate this feature space on a comprehensive benchmark of complex synthetic wavefields and two real-world examples: an Exotic Seismic Events Catalog (ESEC) and a Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) dataset. Spec2VEC provides objective features for information discrimination and enables highly accurate classification of the diverse geophysical signal classes present in the ESEC catalog. Furthermore, application on the high data volume DAS dataset confirms its computational efficiency and domain-agnostic capability to isolate anomalous seismic arrivals from background noise. Ultimately, Spec2VEC bridges the interpretability of classical signal processing with the discriminative power of modern representation learning, providing a reliable, interpretable foundation for automated discovery across the geosciences.

title: AI and Corporate Strategy: HealthCheckAI
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) transforms operational excellence from a slow-moving quality-improvement initiative to a continuous adaptive source of competitive advantage. HealthCheckAI functions more like the human body's own intelligence: constantly sensing, adapting, and evolving without conscious effort. HealthCheckAI transforms organizational operations through three fundamental capabilities to create “evolutionary intelligence”. They are omnidirectional sensing, adaptive simulation, and continuous reconfiguration. Organizations that successfully implement HealthCheckAI transform operational excellence from a static achievement to a dynamic capability, called as operational evolvability. If HealthCheckAI is the organization's operating system for adaptive excellence, Adaptive Risk Intelligence Architecture (ARIA) is its financial immune system. What makes ARIA distinct is its operating environment. Internal risks include compliance failures, communication breakdowns, and data integrity issues. Chief financial officers and Chief risk officers must also manage external risks, from market volatility to shifting regulatory landscapes.

title: Detection of extremely rare dead cells in fluorescence microscopy images
abstract: Dead cell detection in fluorescence microscopy is essential for phenotypic screening and drug efficacy assessment. However, automated identification remains challenging due to signal variability, optical artifacts, and colocalization ambiguities across multiple channels. Markers that define nuclear boundaries do not neatly coincide spatially or temporally with apoptotic markers. Furthermore, marker accumulation kinetics vary across individual cells and apoptosis stages, making universal thresholds unreliable. We present a systematic comparison of several computational approaches for detecting apoptotic cells in nucleus-stained specimens: (1) heuristic methods using intensity thresholds, distributions, correlations, and domain guidance; (2) classification using numerical features (Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost and LightGBM) and image features (ResNet-18 and EfficientNet-B0); and (3) anomaly detection, also using numerical features (Isolation Forest, one-class SVM and PCA reconstruction) and image features (convolutional autoencoders and Deep SVDD). title: MHR-Router: Multimodal Heterogeneous Retrieval-Enhanced Adaptive Routing for VLM Inference
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) exhibit complementary capabilities, yet selecting the most suitable expert for a given image-question query remains challenging due to heterogeneous multimodal inputs and varying expert strengths. Existing routing approaches rely on text-based cues or static model profiles, failing to capture fine-grained visual evidence and expert-specific failure patterns. To address this, we propose MHR-Router, a multimodal heterogeneous retrieval-enhanced adaptive routing framework for VLM inference. It accurately dispatches each multimodal query to the most suitable VLM expert via local retrieval evidence. MHR-Router consists of two stages: (1) Multimodal Routing Representation, which fuses frozen multimodal features into a comprehensive query representation; and (2) Heterogeneous Retrieval-Enhanced Adaptive Routing, which retrieves expert-specific success and failure memories as local evidence and employs a shared scorer to adaptively select the optimal expert. Experiments show that MHR-Router effectively achieves heterogeneous modality routing and consistently improves accuracy over traditional baselines.

title: Redirecting Teacher Supervision: Temporal-Response-Guided Latent Distillation for Video-Language Models
abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers capabilities through teacher predictions on student-generated sequences, as studied by GKD and MiniLLM for language models and Video-OPD for video tasks. We ask how internal supervision can further support temporal learning. Direct hidden-state alignment does not explicitly use the student's temporal responses to choose a supervision direction. We propose Temporal-Response Guidance (TRG), which measures representation responses to local temporal perturbations, adds the teacher correction's projection onto their span back to the original correction, and restores its original norm. The projection is not normalized separately, and correction components outside the response space are retained. With an orthogonal tangent projector and a detached target, TRG changes the supervision direction while preserving the cosine-loss value and aligned-representation gradient norm at target construction. On TempCompass, Video-MME, MVBench, and Video-MMMU, TRG improves the 4B student's macro accuracy by 2.86 percentage points over the reported output-only OPD baseline.

title: Reward Hacking as a Transmissible Strategy in Multi-Agent Coding Systems
abstract: Multi-agent systems are increasingly used to solve coding tasks by coordinating agents that share code and plans. These agents are often optimized with reinforcement learning (RL) using automated evaluators, but bypassing evaluation can earn reward without producing a genuine solution. Prior work has largely treated reward hacking as a single-agent failure. In this work, we show that a reward-hacking strategy elicited in one agent can propagate to others and affect system coordination. Across four open-weight backbones, coding RL elicits and amplifies reward hacking in two settings: explicit mechanism descriptions in the system prompt and mid-training that models upstream exposure to facts about the coding environment. Using post-RL agents from the mid-training setting as sources, we observe propagation through code and shared memory, and across roles through natural-language plans. Even agents based on small open-weight models induce reward hacking in stronger closed-weight targets. On hard tasks, propagation can intensify along a transmission chain after the original source leaves as the code acquires more persuasive justifications. We also theoretically analyze conditions under which reward hacking amplifies, persists, or decays across agent interactions. Beyond propagation, reward hacking can bias task routing toward reward-hacking agents and survive candidate aggregation. As potential mitigations, we evaluate code review by the coder or a separate verifier, both of which reduce delivered hacks. Together, these results establish reward hacking as a transmissible strategy whose effects extend beyond the agent in which it first emerges.

title: Calibration-Aware Patient-Level Prediction of Source-Defined MSIMUT Status in Colorectal Cancer from Whole-Slide Histopathology Images Using Foundation-Model Embeddings
abstract: Background/Objectives: Microsatellite instability (MSI) is clinically important in colorectal cancer, but definitive assessment requires molecular or immunohistochemical testing. This study developed a leakage-safe, calibration-aware patient-level framework for predicting a source-defined MSIMUT category from hematoxylin-and-eosin whole-slide-derived patches using fixed Phikon foundation-model embeddings. Methods: The TCGA-derived colorectal cohort comprised 360 patients, including 65 source-defined positive and 295 MSS cases, represented by 192,312 pre-extracted patches. Patch embeddings were aggregated using mean, max, and mean-plus-max pooling, and downstream classifiers were evaluated under patient-level cross-validation with calibration, threshold, decision-curve, clinicopathological, source-provenance, and patch-count sensitivity analyses. Results: In the primary random patient-level evaluation, logistic regression with mean-plus-max pooling achieved a mean ROC-AUC of 0.915 and PR-AUC of 0.809. Fully nested Platt calibration yielded pooled out-of-sample ROC-AUC 0.913, PR-AUC 0.796, Brier score 0.073, calibration slope 1.037, and calibration-in-the-large 0.023. Within the internally cross-validated mean-plus-max framework, an exploratory sensitivity ≥ 0.95 operating point yielded sensitivity 0.969, specificity 0.393, and negative predictive value 0.983. Provenance reconstruction identified source-partition-dependent patch-count structure. In a source-TRAIN to source-TEST holdout, mean-plus-max ROC-AUC decreased to 0.788, while patch count alone was near chance in source-TEST (ROC-AUC 0.517) and explicit patch-count addition did not improve discrimination. Conclusions: These findings support the methodological feasibility of fixed foundation-model embeddings for internal MSI-related pre-screening research, while showing that apparent performance is sensitive to source structure. Independent multicenter validation with clinically adjudicated MSI-H/dMMR endpoints remains necessary before clinical application.

title: MЕТОД АВТОМАТИЧЕСКОГО РАЗРЕШЕНИЯ ОМОГРАФИИ НА ОСНОВЕ ЕВКЛИДОВОЙ МЕТРИКИ WEN
abstract: В статье проведен обзор классических методов разрешения лексической многозначности, использующих векторное представление слов и евклидово расстояние. Представлен новый метод WSD – метод автоматического разрешения омографии на основе евклидовой метрики. Приведено описание работы метода WEN на примере распознавания омографа «замок» в предложении, показан процесс «оцифровки» слов и предложений из баз, вычисление расстояний от тестового предложения до баз предложений с различными значениями омографа. Представлены данные об экспериментальном исследовании метода WEN на базах предложений с омографами для малоресурсного чеченского языка. Проведено сравнение полученных метрик точности с аналогичными методами для различных языков.
